question.text:
$ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} $

$\displaystyle \int \coth x(2\sinh x + \csch x) \, extrm{d}x = $
question.explanation:
\[ \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\cosh}{\mathop{\rm cosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sinh}{\mathop{\rm sinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \]

First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometry identity

\[ \cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}. \]

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

\[ \coth x = \dfrac{\cosh x}{\sinh x}. \]

Now, we multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity above, as follows:

\begin{align} \int \coth x(2\sinh x + \csch x) \, \textrm{d}x &= \int \left(\coth {x}\cdot 2\sinh{x} + \coth{x} \cdot\csch {x}\right) \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \int \left(\dfrac{\cosh x}{\sinh x}\cdot 2\sinh x + \coth{x}\csch{x} \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int \left(2\cosh{x} + \coth{x}\csch{x}\right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int 2\cosh{x} \, \textrm{d}x + \int \coth{x}\csch{x} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = 2\sinh{x} - \csch x + C \end{align}

question.text:
$ ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} ewcommand{\cosh}{\mathop{ m cosh} olimits} ewcommand{\sinh}{\mathop{ m sinh} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits}$

Evaluate $\displaystyle{\int_{\ln{2}}^{\ln{3}} \dfrac{1}{\sinh^2(2x)} \, extrm{d}x }.$
question.explanation:
$\newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\cosh}{\mathop{\rm cosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sinh}{\mathop{\rm sinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits}$

First, recall the following identity: \[ \csch{x}=\dfrac{1}{\sinh{x}} \]

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows: \[ \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 3} \dfrac{1}{\sinh^2(2x)} \, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 3} \csch^2(2x) \, \textrm{d}x. \end{align} \]

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=2x.$ Then, \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 2 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \dfrac 12 \, \textrm d u = \, \textrm d x. \]

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=2x.$

$x$ $\ln 2$ $\ln 3$
$u$ $\ln 4$ $\ln 9$

Now, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 3} \csch^2(2x) \, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{\ln 4}^{\ln 9} \csch^2 u\,\cdot \dfrac 12 \, \textrm d u\\[5pt] &= \dfrac 12 \int_{\ln 4}^{\ln 9} \csch^2 u\, \textrm d u\\[5pt] &=\dfrac 12 (-\coth u)\Bigg|_{\ln 4}^{\ln 9} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac 12 \left(-\coth(\ln 9)+ \coth (\ln 4)\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac 12 \left(-\dfrac{e^{2\ln 9}+1}{e^{2\ln 9}-1}+ \dfrac{e^{2\ln 4}+1}{e^{2\ln 4}-1}\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac 12 \left(-\dfrac{9^2+1}{9^2-1}+ \dfrac{4^2+1}{4^2-1}\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac 12 \left(-\dfrac{41}{40}+ \dfrac{17}{15}\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{13}{240} } \end{eqnarray}

question.text: $ ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} ewcommand{\cosh}{\mathop{ m cosh} olimits} ewcommand{\sinh}{\mathop{ m sinh} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} \displaystyle \int \sech{x} \left( anh{x} - 2\cosh{x} ight) extrm{d}x =$
question.explanation:
\[ \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\cosh}{\mathop{\rm cosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sinh}{\mathop{\rm sinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \]

First, we recall the following identity: \[ \sech{x} = \dfrac{1}{\cosh{x}} \]

Now, we multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity above, as follows: \begin{align} \int \sech{x} \left(\tanh{x} - 2\cosh{x} \right) \textrm{d}x & = \int (\sech{x}\tanh{x} - \sech{x} \cdot 2\cosh{x}) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \int \left(\sech{x}\tanh{x} - \dfrac{1}{\cosh{x}} \cdot 2 \cosh{x} \right) \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \int \left(\sech{x}\tanh{x} - 2 \right) \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \int \sech{x}\tanh{x} \, \textrm{d}x - \int 2 \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = -\sech{x} - 2x + C \end{align}

example.title: Integrating a Product of Hyperbolic Functions

question.explanation:
\[ \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\cosh}{\mathop{\rm cosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sinh}{\mathop{\rm sinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \] First, we write the integral as \[ \int _{1}^{2} \dfrac{\coth^2{x}}{2\cosh^2 x}\textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\int _{1}^{2} \dfrac{1}{\cosh^2{x}}\cdot \coth^2{x} \, \textrm{d}x. \]

Now we need to find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometric identity

\[ \cot{x}=\dfrac{\cos{x}}{\sin{x}}. \]

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is \[ \coth{x} = \dfrac{\cosh{x}}{\sinh{x}}. \]

Then, we use the above identity to write the integral as follows:

\begin{align} \dfrac{1}{2}\int _{1}^{2} \dfrac{1}{\cosh^2{x}}\cdot \coth^2{x} \, \textrm{d}x &=\dfrac{1}{2} \int _{1}^{2} \dfrac{1}{\cosh^2{x}}\cdot \dfrac{\cosh^2{x}}{\sinh^2{x}} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\int _{1}^{2} \dfrac{\cosh^2{x}}{\cosh^2{x}}\cdot \dfrac{1}{\sinh^2{x}} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\int _{1}^{2} \dfrac{1}{\sinh^2{x}} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{1}^{2} \csch^2{x} \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{2}\coth {x}\Bigg|_{1}^{2}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{2}\coth{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\coth\left(1\right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\coth\left(1\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\coth 2 \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{e^2+1}{e^2-1} - \dfrac{e^4+1}{e^4-1}\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2}\left( \dfrac{(e^2+1)^2-(e^4+1)}{(e^4-1)}\right)\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{e^2}{e^4-1}} \end{align}

example.title: Integrating a Quotient of Hyperbolic Functions

question.explanation:
$\newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\cosh}{\mathop{\rm cosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sinh}{\mathop{\rm sinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits}$

First, we find the hyperbolic identities that correspond to the following trigonometric identities:

\[ \tan{x}=\dfrac{\sin{x}}{\cos{x}}, \quad \sec{x}= \dfrac{1}{\cos{x}} \]

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

\[ \tanh{x}= \dfrac{\sinh{x}}{\cosh{x}}, \quad \sech{x}=\dfrac{1}{\cosh{x}}. \]

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows: \[ \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{0}^{\ln 2} 3\sech(3x)\tanh(3x)\,\textrm d x &= 3\int_{0}^{\ln 2} \sech(3x)\tanh(3x)\,\textrm d x \\[5pt] & = 3\int_{0}^{\ln 2} \dfrac{1}{\cosh(3x)}\cdot \dfrac{\sinh(3x)}{\cosh(3x)}\, \textrm{d}x \end{align} \]

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=3x.$ Then, \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 3 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \textrm d u = 3 \, \textrm d x. \]

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=3x.$

$x$ $0$ $\ln 2$
$u$ $0$ $\ln 8$

Now, we evaluate the integral as follows:

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ 3\int_{0}^{\ln 2} \sech(3x)\tanh(3x) \, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{0}^{\ln 8} \sech(u)\tanh(u)\,\cdot \textrm d u\\[5pt] &=-\sech(u)\Bigg|_{0}^{\ln 8}\\[5pt] &=-\sech(\ln 8)+\sech(0) \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{\cosh(\ln 8)}+1 \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{8+8^{-1}}{2}\right)}+1 \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{65}{16}\right)}+1 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{49}{65}} } \end{eqnarray}
